plugins.name: disciplined-thinking
plugins.description: Core mental models, decision chains, and task routing for structured executive analysis.

plugins.name: delivery-and-flow
plugins.description: Diagnose and improve delivery flow: value streams, WIP, metrics, org design, and portfolio prioritization.

plugins.name: consulting-craft
plugins.description: Executive problem structuring, communication, and consulting engagement discipline.

plugins.name: innovation-strategy
plugins.description: Discover opportunities, validate solutions, and manage an innovation portfolio. Grounded in Lean Startup, Jobs Theory, Continuous Discovery, and Three Horizons.

plugins.name: applied-ai
plugins.description: Govern AI agent deployments, assess autonomy levels, and apply AI authority boundaries in organizational contexts.

plugins.name: leadership
plugins.description: Execute with intent, command with clarity, and learn systematically. Mission Command, OODA Loop, and After-Action Review for senior practitioners.

plugins.name: business-strategy
plugins.description: Diagnose growth constraints, map profit pools, segment customers for strategy decisions, design decision-linked KPI systems, and govern value realization after approval.

chainDescriptionOverrides.pricing-decision: Runs an eight-step pricing decision chain from first principles through experiments and margin of safety. Use when setting or changing prices, packaging, or monetization.
chainDescriptionOverrides.market-entry: Structured market entry analysis: opportunity, defensibility, assumptions, and entry mode. Use when entering a new market, segment, or geography.
chainDescriptionOverrides.hiring-decision: Hiring decision chain: role outcomes, failure modes, evidence, and culture fit. Use for significant hires or role design.
chainDescriptionOverrides.product-launch: Product or feature launch chain: assumptions, readiness, metrics, and failure modes. Use before launches or major releases.
chainDescriptionOverrides.investment-decision: Capital allocation chain: thesis, downside, alternatives, and monitoring. Use for investments of money or strategic capacity.
chainDescriptionOverrides.should-i-quit: Quit-or-stay decision chain separating signal from noise. Use when considering leaving a role, company, or project.
chainDescriptionOverrides.life-decision: Major life decision chain with reversibility and probabilistic scenarios. Use for long-horizon personal or career choices.
chainDescriptionOverrides.capacity-planning: Eight-step capacity planning chain before committing resources. Use when planning team or portfolio capacity.
chainDescriptionOverrides.transformation: Organizational transformation readiness and sequencing chain. Use for large change programs.
chainDescriptionOverrides.improve-delivery-flow: Eight-step flow improvement chain: VSM, bottlenecks, WIP, forecasting, metrics, PDCA. Use for slow delivery, missed dates, or flow reviews.
chainDescriptionOverrides.org-design-for-flow: Org design diagnostic chain: value stream, team topologies, Conway, dependencies. Use when structure blocks flow.
chainDescriptionOverrides.work-to-be-done: Ten-step chain from outcome through theory of change, MECE work tree, prioritization, and capacity check. Use when scoping what must be built or delivered before execution.
chainDescriptionOverrides.innovation-capability-diagnostic: Diagnoses an organization's innovation capability across culture, process, portfolio, and metrics. Use when an innovation programme is underperforming or before designing one.
chainDescriptionOverrides.design-launch-innovation-program: End-to-end chain for designing and launching an innovation programme: mandate, structure, portfolio, governance, and metrics. Use when commissioning or redesigning innovation capability.
chainDescriptionOverrides.from-idea-to-hypothesis: Converts a raw idea into a testable hypothesis with explicit assumptions, success criteria, and a minimum viable experiment. Use before committing any resources to a new initiative.
chainDescriptionOverrides.crawl-walk-run: Stages a new initiative across three evidence gates — does it work at all (crawl), well enough (walk), with real economics (run). Use to de-risk innovation bets and prevent premature scaling.
chainDescriptionOverrides.ai-agent-governance-design: Designs the governance structure for an AI agent deployment: authority levels, escalation paths, monitoring, and override protocols. Use when deploying autonomous AI in a business context.
chainDescriptionOverrides.ai-use-case-autonomy-assessment: Assesses the appropriate autonomy level for a proposed AI use case using reversibility, consequence severity, and human-in-loop criteria. Use before approving AI agent scope or expanding AI authority.
chainDescriptionOverrides.mission-execution-protocol: Structures mission execution from commander's intent through brief-back, execution cadence, and after-action review. Use for high-stakes projects requiring disciplined command and control.
chainDescriptionOverrides.organisational-degradation-scan: Seven-step diagnostic for why an organisation is quietly underperforming. Covers drift, scale threshold, bureaucratic expansion, management competence, metric capture, structural lock-in, and incentive misalignment. Run before launching any transformation programme.

toolkits.description: Maps value stream, finds bottlenecks and queue delay, estimates cycle time from WIP and throughput. Use for slow delivery, missed dates, everyone busy, or executive lead-time questions.
deliverableSections: Executive summary (3 bullets)
Current-state flow map (steps, wait times, handoffs)
Bottleneck hypothesis and evidence
Flow efficiency estimate and implication
Little's Law check (WIP, throughput, predicted cycle time)
Recommended next intervention

toolkits.description: Designs WIP limits, pull policies, and flow-based commitments. Use when starting kanban, breaking WIP limits, or defining lead-time promises.
deliverableSections: Current WIP and pain points
Proposed WIP limits per stage (with rationale)
Explicit pull and swarm policies
Lead time vs cycle time definitions for stakeholders
Rollout plan and expected trade-offs

toolkits.description: Defines delivery and flow metrics, variability, and probabilistic forecasts. Use for dashboards, predictability, SLA design, or executive reporting.
deliverableSections: Metric set (definitions, owners, cadence)
Baseline and target percentiles (not averages only)
Forecast range with assumptions
Goodhart risks (how metrics could be gamed)
Review ritual recommendation

toolkits.description: Aligns teams and dependencies to value streams using team topologies and Conway. Use for reorgs, platform teams, or cross-team blocking work.
deliverableSections: Value stream and primary constraint
Current org vs desired topology
Dependency map (critical paths)
Inverse Conway moves (team changes to get desired flow)
Risks and transition sequencing

toolkits.description: Prioritizes work under scarce capacity using cost of delay, WSJF, and kill criteria. Use for portfolio debates, roadmaps, or what to stop.
deliverableSections: Scarcity constraint (what is the real bottleneck)
Ranked initiatives with cost-of-delay rationale
What to stop or defer (kill criteria applied)
Single explicit focus recommendation
Governance check (funding, WIP at portfolio level)

toolkits.description: Structures ambiguous problems with MECE issue trees and hypothesis-driven consulting. Use for steering committees, problem statements, or issue trees.
deliverableSections: Problem statement (one sentence)
MECE issue tree (top level 3–5 branches)
Key hypotheses to test
Evidence plan per hypothesis
What would falsify the leading hypothesis

toolkits.description: Produces answer-first executive communication using the pyramid principle. Use for board decks, exec memos, or steering updates.
deliverableSections: Governing thought (answer first)
Supporting arguments (MECE)
Evidence per argument
So-what and ask
Optional appendix structure

toolkits.description: Frames consulting engagements: lifecycle, scope, and contracting. Use when scoping work, SOWs, or diagnose-design-deliver-detach.
deliverableSections: Engagement phase and objective
Scope in / scope out
Success criteria and measures
Client vs consultant responsibilities
Exit and knowledge transfer criteria

toolkits.description: Applies core mental models (first principles, inversion, incentives, bottlenecks, bias checks) to the user's situation. Use for ambiguous decisions, strategy, or when no specialized chain fits.
deliverableSections: Situation summary
Primary model lens used and why
Analysis (3–5 insights)
Checking models applied
Recommended action and risks

toolkits.description: Applies problem-space discovery models to understand what is worth working on and for whom. Grounded in Jobs Theory, Customer Development, Design Thinking, and Continuous Discovery. Use before any solution work begins.
deliverableSections: Customer segment and context (who, doing what, under what conditions)
Job-to-be-done statement (functional, emotional, social dimensions)
Opportunity map (pains, gains, unmet needs — using OST structure)
Assumptions that must be true for this opportunity to be real
Recommended next discovery move (interview, observation, or prototype)

toolkits.description: Designs and sequences experiments to validate a solution hypothesis with minimum effort. Grounded in Pretotyping, MVP, Build-Measure-Learn, and the Experiment Ladder. Use when moving from problem to solution space.
deliverableSections: Hypothesis to test (if we do X, we expect Y, because Z)
Riskiest assumption (what must be true for this to work)
Experiment type and rationale (pretotype → MVP → scaled test)
Success criteria and falsification threshold
What to build, measure, and learn — in that sequence

toolkits.description: Allocates innovation investment across time horizons and measures portfolio health. Grounded in Three Horizons, Innovation Accounting, and Innovation Health Indicators. Use for portfolio reviews, programme design, or executive reporting on innovation.
deliverableSections: Current portfolio mapped across Horizon 1 / 2 / 3 (with investment %)
Portfolio balance assessment (over-indexed on any horizon?)
Innovation health indicators — current state vs target
Innovation Accounting metrics (validated learning, cohort progress)
Recommended portfolio rebalancing and governance changes

toolkits.description: Applies AI authority boundaries, minimal capability principle, and prompt injection defences to a proposed AI deployment. Use when scoping an AI agent, reviewing autonomy levels, or designing safety guardrails.
deliverableSections: Proposed AI scope and autonomy level
Authority boundaries (what the agent may and may not do)
Minimal capability assessment (is scope narrower than necessary?)
Prompt injection and adversarial input risks
Human-in-loop requirements and override protocols

toolkits.description: Structures commander's intent, delegates with clarity, and maintains alignment during execution. Grounded in Mission Command, Leader's Intent, Brief-Back Protocols, and OODA Loop. Use for high-stakes projects, operational leadership, or when delegating to autonomous teams.
deliverableSections: Commander's intent (purpose, end-state, key constraints — one paragraph)
Delegated tasks and decision authority per role
Brief-back summary (what each lead will do and why — in their words)
OODA cadence (observe-orient-decide-act cycle and trigger conditions)
Red lines and escalation protocol

toolkits.description: Runs structured learning reviews after significant events, decisions, or project phases. Grounded in After-Action Review, Three-Question Ritual, and Tactical Pause. Use after any high-stakes event to extract lessons and adjust.
deliverableSections: What was intended vs what actually happened
Three-question ritual output (what worked / what didn't / what to change)
Root causes (not surface symptoms)
Lessons to institutionalise (changes to process, doctrine, or assumptions)
Follow-up owners and deadlines

toolkits.description: Diagnoses why an organisation is quietly underperforming. Covers drift, scale threshold, bureaucratic expansion, management layer quality, metric capture, and incentive misalignment. Use when leadership senses something is wrong but cannot name it, or before launching a transformation programme.
deliverableSections: Primary degradation mechanism (name it and explain why it is primary)
Evidence for each active mechanism (drift / scale / Parkinson / Peter / Goodhart / Conway / agency)
Compounding sequence (how the mechanisms reinforce each other)
What is individually rational but collectively corrosive
Intervention priority and what comes next (Transformation Chain or Org Design for Flow)

toolkits.description: Scans a change programme or innovation initiative for Cobra Effect risk: whether the intervention is sustaining the problem it was designed to solve. Use before launching programmes, or when a running programme shows activity but no outcome improvement.
deliverableSections: Programme description and stated goal
Cobra type classification (metric / gate removal / psych safety / innovation unit / incentive realignment)
Pre-launch cobra risk assessment (5 questions answered)
Current metric performance vs underlying outcome performance
Redesign recommendation or kill criteria

toolkits.description: Scans a decision, analysis, or plan for active cognitive biases. Covers anchoring, availability, survivorship, hindsight, planning fallacy, fundamental attribution error, base rate neglect, social proof, and Dunning-Kruger. Use before committing to a decision, after a surprising outcome, or when a recommendation feels too clean.
deliverableSections: Decision or analysis under review (one sentence)
Active biases identified (name each, with evidence it is operating)
Highest-risk bias (the one most likely to distort the outcome)
Structural mitigations (specific process changes, not just awareness)
Revised confidence level after bias audit

toolkits.description: Stress-tests a plan, belief, or decision by applying structured adversarial challenge. Covers pre-mortem, steelmanning, red teaming, calibration, falsification, two-way doors, and Cynefin domain classification. Use before high-stakes commitments, when a recommendation feels too certain, or when a team has converged without genuine challenge.
deliverableSections: Plan or belief under review (one sentence)
Domain classification (Cynefin: clear / complicated / complex / chaotic)
Pre-mortem: top 3 failure modes with estimated probability
Steelman: strongest case against the plan
Calibration audit: stated confidence vs. track record evidence
Reversibility assessment (two-way door or one-way door)
What would have to be true for this to be wrong (falsification test)
Recommended changes before committing

toolkits.description: Analyses competitive position, market structure, and strategic options. Covers Wardley Mapping, Kernel of Good Strategy, Scenario Planning, Network Effects, Power Law, Long Tail, Nash Equilibrium, and Path Dependence. Use when assessing competitive threats, designing market strategy, evaluating platform or marketplace opportunities, or stress-testing a strategic plan.
deliverableSections: Strategic question under review (one sentence)
Landscape map: where components sit on the evolution axis (genesis → commodity)
Market structure: power law or long tail? Winner-take-most or niche-viable?
Network effects assessment: do you have them, how strong, what sustains them?
Nash Equilibrium analysis: what is the stable end-state and is it where you want to be?
Path dependence: what are you locked into, what is the competitor locked into?
Scenarios: 2-3 plausible futures and the strategy that survives each
Strategic recommendation: kernel (diagnosis, guiding policy, coherent actions)

toolkits.description: Analyses system behaviour, tipping points, and tail risk. Covers Feedback Loops, Margin of Safety, S-Curves, Red Queen Dilemma, Emergence, Critical Mass, and Black Swan. Use when a system is behaving unexpectedly, when assessing structural risk, when evaluating a platform or network approaching a tipping point, or when a risk model may be missing catastrophic scenarios.

branches.label: Assess tipping points and competitive escalation

deliverableSections: System description and the presenting behaviour or concern
Loop map: dominant reinforcing and balancing loops, with delays identified
S-curve position: where is the system on the adoption/growth curve?
Tipping point assessment: is critical mass near, and what triggers it?
Red Queen check: is escalation locked in, and what breaks the cycle?
Tail risk assessment: what Black Swan events would this system not survive?
Margin of safety: is the current buffer sized to survive the tail, not just the average?
Leverage point: where is the highest-return intervention in the system?

toolkits.description: Maps stakeholder landscape and designs an influence strategy for situations where formal authority is insufficient. Covers power mapping, stakeholder salience, influence without authority, coalition building, framing, reciprocity, Overton Window, and commitment dynamics. Use before any significant initiative, when a proposal keeps hitting resistance, or when you need to move something through an organisation without rank.
deliverableSections: Initiative or change requiring influence (one sentence)
Power map: decision-makers, influencers, blockers, and their interests
Overton Window assessment: is the proposal currently inside or outside the window?
Coalition design: minimum winning coalition with sequencing
Framing strategy: how to position the ask for each key stakeholder
Reciprocity audit: what credibility and goodwill has been built with each target?
Commitment pathway: early small asks that create consistency pressure toward the main ask
Recommended next move and timing

toolkits.description: Designs and sequences a change initiative, with emphasis on the psychological and structural barriers that cause well-designed changes to fail. Covers Change Management (Kotter), Immunity to Change, Activation Energy, Narrative Instinct, Theory of Change, Framing, and Commitment & Consistency Bias. Use when launching any significant change: cultural, structural, process, or behavioural.
deliverableSections: Change goal and current state (one paragraph)
Immunity to Change diagnosis: what competing commitments are protecting the status quo?
Activation energy map: what friction must be removed to make the first step easy?
Theory of Change: the causal chain from intervention to desired outcome
Narrative strategy: the story that makes the change feel necessary and possible
Kotter sequencing: which steps are complete, which are missing
Commitment pathway: early wins and public commitments that build consistency pressure
Failure mode most likely to kill this change, and its mitigation

toolkits.description: Builds a clear understanding of a complex or ambiguous situation before prescribing action. Covers Ladder of Inference, Causal Analysis, Occam's Razor, Hanlon's Razor, Analogical Reasoning, and SRK Framework. Use as the entry point when the situation is unclear, when a diagnosis has been handed to you and you want to verify it, or when a team is jumping to solutions before the problem is understood.
deliverableSections: Presenting situation (what has been observed — facts only, no interpretation)
Ladder of Inference audit: where are conclusions outrunning evidence?
Causal map: proximate causes vs root causes, with evidence for each link
Occam's Razor check: what is the simplest explanation consistent with the evidence?
Hanlon's Razor check: is this better explained by incompetence or misaligned incentives than intent?
Analogous situations: what comparable cases exist and what did they reveal?
SRK classification: is this a skill-based, rule-based, or knowledge-based problem?
Diagnosis (one sentence) and confidence level

toolkits.description: Diagnoses why a person or team is behaving in a particular way and designs interventions that work with human motivation rather than against it. Covers Trust, Psychological Safety, Self-Determination Theory, Organisational Culture, Purpose Clarity, and McClelland's Acquired Needs. Use when a person or team is underperforming, disengaged, or resistant, and the structural and incentive explanations have been ruled out.
deliverableSections: Person or team and the presenting behaviour
McClelland needs profile: achievement / affiliation / power — which dominates?
SDT assessment: are autonomy, competence, and relatedness present or absent?
Trust audit: cognitive trust (competence) and affective trust (intention) — where is the gap?
Psychological safety level: what is safe to say and what is not?
Culture diagnosis: what does the organisation actually reward and punish (not what it says)?
Purpose clarity check: can this person state in one sentence why their work matters?
Recommended intervention and what to avoid

toolkits.description: Assesses whether a dataset, analysis, or recommendation should be trusted. Covers Sampling, Regression to the Mean, Randomness, Observer Bias, A/B Testing, and Experiment Design. Use when evaluating data presented to support a decision, when reviewing a consultant's analysis, or when designing evidence-gathering.
deliverableSections: Analysis or dataset under review
Sampling audit: is the sample representative? What is excluded?
Regression to the mean check: is an extreme result being mistaken for a real effect?
Randomness check: is the pattern real or noise given the sample size?
Observer bias audit: did the evaluator know which group was which?
Experiment design quality: was success pre-specified? Was there a control?
Confidence verdict: should this analysis be trusted, and at what confidence level?

toolkits.description: Designs a communication for maximum clarity and impact. Covers Narrative Instinct, Grice's Maxims, Audience, Framing, and Ladder of Inference. Use when preparing a recommendation, briefing, presentation, or any communication where the quality of the message determines whether good thinking gets acted on.
deliverableSections: Communication goal: what decision or action should this message produce?
Audience profile: what do they know, what do they care about, what would stop them acting?
Grice's audit: is every element necessary? Is anything missing that the audience needs?
Narrative structure: situation → complication → resolution (or equivalent)
Framing choice: gain or loss frame? Which reference point serves the goal?
Ladder of Inference check: are conclusions clearly separated from evidence?
Revised message (one paragraph lead, supporting structure)

toolkits.description: Evaluates how to allocate resources across competing opportunities or initiatives. Covers Asymmetry/Convexity, Regret Minimization Framework, Kill Criteria, Unit Economics, and OKRs. Use for portfolio-level decisions: which bets to make, which to kill, and how to size each. Distinct from the single investment-decision chain.
deliverableSections: Portfolio under review: list of current initiatives or investment options
Asymmetry audit: for each bet, is downside bounded and upside open-ended?
Unit economics check: does each bet have sound economics per unit at current scale?
Regret minimization: which decisions will be regretted most if not taken? Which if taken?
Kill criteria: what pre-specified conditions trigger stopping each initiative?
OKR alignment: do current initiatives map to the outcomes that matter most?
Portfolio recommendation: what to fund, size, and kill

toolkits.description: Structures a negotiation or deal-making situation. Covers Schelling Points, Prisoner's Dilemma, Anchoring, Loss Aversion, and Reciprocity. Use for commercial negotiations, partnership deals, internal resource allocation disputes, or any situation where two parties must reach agreement.
deliverableSections: Negotiation context: parties, stakes, and time horizon
Game structure: is this a one-shot or repeated game? Zero-sum or positive-sum?
Prisoner's Dilemma check: is mutual defection a risk? What enables commitment?
Schelling Point analysis: what focal points exist and who controls the salience-setting?
Anchor strategy: what opening position creates the most favourable reference point?
Loss framing opportunity: how can the proposal be framed around what the other party stands to lose?
Reciprocity pathway: what concession can be made first to create an obligation to reciprocate?
Recommended opening position and negotiation sequence

toolkits.description: Builds a fact-based, MECE current-state baseline across financial, market, customer, competitive, operating, and organizational lenses before anyone debates what to do. Use before strategy conversations, steering committees, or any 'what's actually going on?' question — and always before solutioning begins.
deliverableSections: Presenting question (the problem as stated, before the assessment)
Fact base by lens (financial, market, customer, competitive, operating, organizational — facts only)
Momentum read (trend and rate of change, not just snapshot)
Interpretations (clearly separated from facts) and open questions
Issues list (the 2–3 facts the decision actually turns on)
Implications and the next diagnostic question — no recommendation

toolkits.description: Builds a driver tree across acquisition, activation, conversion, retention, expansion, monetization, and capacity to locate the single binding constraint behind stalled growth, and converts the diagnosis into a test rather than a launch. Use when growth has stalled and the team is reaching for a list of plausible levers instead of a diagnosis.
deliverableSections: Growth gap (size and shape — tuning problem or structural problem?)
Driver tree (acquisition → activation → conversion → retention → expansion → monetization → capacity)
Evidence at each node (quantified breaks, not impressions)
Binding constraint diagnosis (the one or two nodes that would move the topline most)
Root cause vs. symptom check
Cheapest test to confirm the leading hypothesis before committing resources

toolkits.description: Maps where profit — not revenue — concentrates and leaks across a market, value chain, or product set, and explains structurally why it sits where it does. Use for where-to-play decisions, portfolio reviews, or whenever a strategy conversation is anchored on revenue share rather than profit capture.
deliverableSections: Unit of analysis (and why it matches the decision being made)
Revenue pool map (where the money flows)
Profit pool map (where the money stays — side by side with revenue)
Structural explanation of concentration (scale, pricing power, switching costs, cost position, competitive intensity)
Leakage points (value created but captured elsewhere)
Where-to-play / where-to-avoid / how-to-improve-capture recommendation

toolkits.description: Builds MECE customer segments around decision-relevant differences — needs, economics, behavior, strategic value — and scores them on attractiveness and right to win, so targeting, pricing, and roadmap choices can be made deliberately. Use for strategy-level segmentation decisions, not customer discovery.
deliverableSections: Decision this segmentation must inform (pricing, targeting, roadmap, coverage, retention investment)
Segment definitions (MECE, observable/testable — not aspirational)
What predicts behavior in each segment (needs, economics, behavior — not demographics alone)
Attractiveness and right-to-win scoring per segment
The 'does anything actually differ?' test applied to each pair of segments
Targeting, pricing, and roadmap implications — and when to re-segment

toolkits.description: Designs a lean, decision-linked measurement system by working backward from the decisions leaders must make to a driver tree of outcome, driver, and leading-indicator metrics — each with an owner, threshold, and review cadence. Use when a dashboard has grown by accretion, when metrics no longer drive action, or when designing measurement for a new initiative.
deliverableSections: Decisions this system must serve (who decides what, on what cadence)
Driver tree (outcome → the 2–3 drivers that move it → leading indicators)
Metric set: outcome / driver / activity — separated and weighted accordingly
Owner and action threshold per metric (or remove it)
Goodhart risk per metric (how it could be gamed, and the guardrail)
Review cadence and what triggers escalation

toolkits.description: Builds a value ledger — baseline, target, owner, proof standard, and governance rhythm — that tracks whether a strategy, acquisition, or transformation actually delivers the benefits its business case promised. Use at the moment of approval, not eighteen months later, for any initiative whose case will eventually be checked against reality.
deliverableSections: Expected benefits (named individually, with baseline measured before start)
Value ledger (benefit, baseline, target, timing, owner — of the value, not the activity)
One-time vs. recurring benefit treatment (and how each will be re-proven over time)
Proof standard (what would distinguish 'this caused it' from 'it would have happened anyway')
Governance rhythm and escalation trigger (what happens when the benefit is behind plan)
Expected gap vs. business case, and what would justify revising the plan

toolkits.description: Plans the individual, sequenced conversations that move stakeholders to 'yes' before the formal decision meeting — mapping the approval path, the belief gap each person has, and the order in which to engage them. Use before any consequential recommendation reaches a steering committee, board, or approval meeting.
deliverableSections: Decision path (who must say yes, in what order, and what a 'no' from each does to the decision)
Belief gap per stakeholder (what they need to believe — not just know — and why they don't yet)
Engagement sequence (who to talk to first, and why that conversation makes the next one easier)
What each resistant stakeholder's concern will visibly change in the final recommendation
Objections rehearsed in advance (the version of resistance each pre-wiring conversation is expected to surface)
Readiness check: is this meeting now a ratification, or still a persuasion event?

toolkits.description: Applies the integrated MBB operating posture — answer-first, hypothesis-led, MECE structure, 80/20 focus, and decision-orientation — as a single default mode for engaging an ambiguous problem, rather than as five separate techniques. Use as the meta-discipline check before or during any consulting-style engagement, especially when the work feels structured but isn't converging.
deliverableSections: Decision this work is for (the filter that runs first)
Day-one answer (the hypothesis you'd commit to if forced to answer today)
MECE decomposition of that hypothesis into testable sub-claims
Branches ranked by how much each would close the gap if true (the 80/20 cut)
Evidence plan sized to the ranking — not spread evenly across all branches
Answer-first output: headline first, then the structure that supports or revises it

toolkits.description: Designs the day-to-day operating rhythms that protect thinking time and ensure consistent learning and decision quality. Covers Maker's Schedule vs Manager's Schedule, Async-First Default, Three-Question Ritual, After-Action Review, and Attention Budget. Use when a leader's calendar is consuming their capacity to think, when meetings produce no decisions, or when projects end without extracting their lessons.
deliverableSections: Current operating pattern: time allocation across maker work / manager work / coordination
Maker's Schedule audit: how many deep-work blocks per week are uninterrupted?
Async-first assessment: which recurring meetings could be replaced with async communication?
Attention budget: what is consuming attention that is not the highest-value work?
After-Action Review rhythm: is structured learning happening after significant events?
Recommended redesign: specific calendar and rhythm changes with rationale

routers.description: Classifies the user's task and routes to the best chain or toolkit skill. Use at the start of ambiguous consulting, delivery, executive, innovation, AI, or leadership requests.
